title: Minimum Commands for Racecar
prompt:
Implement `racecar(target: int) -> int`. The car starts at position `0` with speed `+1`. Command `A` first moves by the current speed and then doubles that speed. Command `R` leaves position unchanged and replaces a positive speed with `-1`, or a negative speed with `+1`. Return the fewest commands needed to reach the nonnegative integer `target` exactly. Return `0` for target `0`.

Targets of the form `2^k - 1` are reached by `k` consecutive accelerations. For other targets, a dynamic-programming solution can compare overshooting once and reversing with stopping short, reversing, backing up for a chosen number of accelerations, and reversing again. Support targets through at least `10_000`.

A standard bottom-up dynamic program examines a logarithmic number of undershoot choices for each value through `target`, so describe it honestly as `O(target log target)` time and `O(target)` space rather than promising a stronger bound it does not meet.

example.reasoning: One optimal command sequence reaches position 6 in five commands; it is not necessary to enumerate every reachable position when using the dynamic-programming recurrence.
